title: Decision: the keyed call extends draft-atwood-jmap-vtc rather than a fresh document
description:
Mark decided 2026-11-23, for bead mimid-1wgh.114.2.

THE QUESTION. The agent needs a client-facing surface for a keyed call:
start one, see one, get the epoch's media secret. Extend
draft-atwood-jmap-vtc, or write something fresh?

I FIRST ANSWERED FROM A REMEMBERED NOTE and stopped, because that is the
mistake that produced the §5.10 misdesign an hour earlier (bead
mimid-1wgh.114.1). Reading the draft changed the answer from a guess to
evidence.

WHAT THE DRAFT ACTUALLY IS: ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec/
draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00.md, 2394 lines, a complete object model, not a
sketch. VTCCall, VTCParticipant, VTCGateway, VTCMediaState, VTCCallPolicy,
VTCRecording, VTCLivestream; three call types (ring, room, scheduled)
with a server-enforced state machine; methods, push, a Capability
section, and a "# End-to-End Encrypted Calls" section.

THE THREE FINDINGS THAT SETTLE IT:

1. IT LEAVES KEYING TO THE MEDIA LAYER, deliberately. Of e2eeEnabled:
   "The mechanism (WebRTC Encoded Transform, SFrame, or other) is
   media-layer-defined; this field is the state signal for client UI
   (e.g., displaying a lock icon)." So the draft is signalling, with a
   seam exactly where draft-atwood-mimi-calls' media_secret belongs.
   Nothing has to be displaced.
2. ITS COMPANION GUIDE ALREADY SAYS MLS. jmap-vtc-e2ee-guide.md §3 is
   titled "Key management: MLS is the answer for groups", and its
   "Mapping MLS to VTC participant lifecycle" table reads: participant
   joins -> MLS Add + Commit, leaves or kicked -> MLS Remove + Commit,
   "Call ends -> MLS group destroyed". §6 is "Breakout rooms and key
   isolation", which is the same conclusion as bead mimid-96tt's: a call
   among a subset needs its own group. The design was written down
   already; bead mimid-1wgh.108 is its MIMI-side realisation.
3. chatId IS AN OPTIONAL BINDING FIELD, as decision mimid-1wgh.113
   assumed when it chose both a primitive and a convenience. §"Optional
   Binding Fields": "the id of a Chat associated with this call. null if
   the call has no chat binding." That assumption was made from a note
   and is now checked.

CHOSEN: extend it. The gap is narrow and nameable -- how a VTCCall
relates to a MIMI call room, and how a client gets media_secret -- not a
new object model. Writing fresh would duplicate 2394 lines to add two
things.

THE NUANCE THAT MUST BE RECORDED, because it cuts against decision
mimid-1wgh.117 on its face: the draft's state machine is server-enforced
and authoritative, "active" -> "ended" on "All participants leave or a
moderator ends the call", with "ended" terminal. Decision mimid-1wgh.117
says liveness is not knowable remotely. Both are true, of different
people:

- A PARTICIPANT's agent is a member of the call room, sees its
  membership, and can hold authoritative state. The draft's state
  machine is right for them.
- SOMEONE WHO READ THE CHAT ANNOUNCEMENT AND NEVER JOINED has an agent
  that is not in the call room and can learn nothing about it. A VTCCall
  object on their agent cannot carry a trustworthy state, only what the
  announcement said.

So mimid DOES model call state, for calls it is in. Decision
mimid-1wgh.117 is about the cross-provider announcement, not a claim that
mimid never models liveness. The surface must not present a VTCCall state
for a call the agent has not joined as though it were observed.

WRITING IT NEEDS MARK'S PER-WRITE OK: AGENTS.md requires it for every
write to ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec, one approval per write. And no JMAP
reaches the MIMI working group (memory no-jmap-to-the-mimi-wg):
draft-atwood-mimi-calls says where the secret comes from and must stay
silent about this surface.
close_reason: Mark 2026-11-23: extend draft-atwood-jmap-vtc; the draft already leaves keying to the media layer and its guide already names MLS.
